Latin word

magnopere

magnopere (magnō opere)

adverb

greatly, very much; earnestly

In this lexicon

  • a lot

    also used · classical · Cic. Fam. 15.14.4: ego tibi Rōmam properandum magnō opere cēnseō (Lewis & Short); Caes. BG 2.5: magnopere cohortātus (Lewis & Short)

Notes

  1. 1magnopere: short final e (Lewis & Short magnŏpĕrē, marking it like an adverb in -ē). The ablative of opus, which ends in a short -e like every third-declension ablative: the phrase magnō opere written as one word, as the manuscripts of Terence and Cicero still divide it, and as maximō opere, majōre opere show (Lewis & Short, s.v.).
